name: gnosis-vpn
title: Gnosis VPN dashboard
description: Who uses Gnosis VPN, how much traffic it carries and where, read from a Blokli index of the HOPR network. Needs a Blokli database as its data source, and the exit addresses in the list "exits" (Settings → Lists).

lists.name: exits
lists.description: Exit node addresses, per data source. Downstream volume counts only the exits listed here.

queries.title: Block time
queries.description: Fragment: the time of a block, estimated from Gnosis Chain's five-second cadence, counted back from the last block the index has seen.
queries.sql:
-- The time of block {{$block}}, estimated: Gnosis Chain keeps a steady
-- five-second cadence, so counting back from the last indexed block (taken
-- as now) is off by the indexer's lag, seconds at most.
to_timestamp(
  extract(epoch FROM now())
  - (
    (SELECT last_indexed_block FROM chain_info ORDER BY id LIMIT 1)
    - ({{$block}})
  ) * 5
)

queries.title: Hex
queries.description: Expression fragment: bytes as a 0x-prefixed hex string. {{> hex(address)}}.
queries.sql:
-- Bytes as 0x-prefixed hex text, the way addresses are read everywhere.
--
--   {{> hex(account.chain_key)}}   →   '0x6b3c…'
'0x' || encode({{$value = '\x00ff'::bytea}}, 'hex')

queries.title: uint256
queries.description: Expression fragment: a 32-byte big-endian integer as an exact numeric. {{> uint256(balance)}}.
queries.sql:
-- An unsigned big-endian integer of up to 32 bytes — how Blokli stores token
-- amounts — as an exact numeric. Read four bytes at a time, since no integer
-- type holds 256 bits.
--
--   {{> uint256(balance)}}   →   171260453116000000000000
(
  SELECT SUM(
    ('x' || SUBSTRING(LPAD(encode({{$value = '\x0de0b6b3a7640000'::bytea}}, 'hex'), 64, '0') FROM 8 * i + 1 FOR 8))::bit(32)::bigint::numeric
    * (4294967296::numeric ^ (7 - i))
  )
  FROM generate_series(0, 7) AS i
)

queries.title: Decode winning probability
queries.description: Expression fragment: the 7-byte encoded winning probability as a number between 0 and 1.
queries.sql:
-- HOPR's 7-byte winning probability as a number from 0 to 1.
--
-- As hopr-types' WinningProbability::as_f64 does it: read big-endian, add
-- one, and keep the top 52 bits as the mantissa of a float in [1, 2), less
-- one. That is ((v + 1) >> 4) / 2^52 — exact in double precision, and 0 and 1
-- for the all-zero and all-ones encodings.
--
--   {{> decode-win-prob(value)}}   →   0.2
((('x' || encode({{$value = '\xffffffffffffff'::bytea}}, 'hex'))::bit(56)::bigint + 1) >> 4)::float8
  / 4503599627370496

queries.title: VPN nodes
queries.description: Fragment: every announced node (relays and exits), with its account id and address.
queries.sql:
-- Accounts that announced an address: the network's infrastructure, relays
-- and exits alike. Nothing on chain tells the two apart; the exits are the
-- ones named in Settings → Exits ({{list:exits}}).
SELECT account.id AS account_id, account.chain_key AS address
FROM account
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM announcement WHERE announcement.account_id = account.id
)

queries.title: VPN clients
queries.description: Fragment: every account that never announced — the VPN clients — with the block it was deployed in.
queries.sql:
-- VPN clients: accounts that bound a key but never announced an address, so
-- they are not infrastructure. Blokli creates the account row from the
-- KeyBinding event, so its block is when the client was deployed.
SELECT
  account.id AS account_id,
  account.chain_key AS client,
  account.published_block AS deployed_block
FROM account
WHERE account.id NOT IN (SELECT account_id FROM {{> vpn-nodes}} AS node)

queries.title: Oracle updates
queries.description: Fragment: every winning-probability and ticket-price update from the oracle logs, raw value and position.
queries.sql:
-- Every update of the two oracle values the dashboard prices traffic with,
-- oldest first: `ticket-price` (value: the new price, 32 bytes, in wei) and
-- `win-prob` (value: the new winning probability, 7 bytes; decode it with
-- {{> decode-win-prob(value)}}).
--
-- Blokli keeps only the latest of each, in chain_info, so the history is read
-- back from the raw logs. Topics are concatenated 32-byte words, so the first
-- is the event signature:
--
--   TicketPriceUpdated(uint256,uint256)  d4c5e06b…f3fb
--   WinProbUpdated(uint56,uint56)        02728c4a…3800
--
-- Neither event indexes its arguments, so data word 1 is the new value: the
-- price is the whole word, at offset 33; a uint56 is right-aligned in its
-- word, so the probability is its last 7 bytes, at offset 58. The signatures
-- are matched as prefix ranges, which an index on `topics` can answer.
SELECT
  block_number,
  tx_index,
  log_index,
  CASE
    WHEN topics < '\x02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3801'::bytea
      THEN 'win-prob'
    ELSE 'ticket-price'
  END AS kind,
  CASE
    WHEN topics < '\x02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3801'::bytea
      THEN SUBSTRING(data FROM 58 FOR 7)
    ELSE SUBSTRING(data FROM 33 FOR 32)
  END AS value
FROM log
WHERE removed = FALSE
  AND OCTET_LENGTH(data) >= 64
  AND (
    (
      topics >= '\xd4c5e06b1ae097ba02372652a7adaa6e4a8e00be527497a3ad0ebc3f761ef3fb'::bytea
      AND topics < '\xd4c5e06b1ae097ba02372652a7adaa6e4a8e00be527497a3ad0ebc3f761ef3fc'::bytea
    )
    OR (
      topics >= '\x02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3800'::bytea
      AND topics < '\x02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3801'::bytea
    )
  )
ORDER BY block_number, tx_index, log_index

queries.title: VPN redemptions
queries.description: Fragment: every ticket redemption that carried VPN traffic, upstream or downstream, with its block and tickets.
queries.sql:
-- Ticket redemptions that carried Gnosis VPN traffic, one row each.
--
-- Blokli writes one channel_state row per on-chain channel event. Only a
-- TicketRedeemed event advances ticket_index, so a row whose index is above
-- its predecessor's, in the same epoch, marks a redemption on that channel.
-- The jump is not the tickets redeemed: a client numbers a ticket for every
-- packet and only winners are redeemed, so it estimates the packets paid for.
--
-- Payment follows the sender of each hop and a packet's destination is never
-- paid, so one VPN session leaves two paid hops on chain:
--
--   upstream     a client — an account that never announced — paying a relay
--   downstream   one of the network's configured exits paying a relay for
--                the answer
--
-- Everything else on these channels is announced nodes ({{> vpn-nodes}})
-- probing each other, and is left out. Exits are read from Settings → Exits
-- ({{list:exits}}); none configured means no downstream at all rather than a guess.
--
-- The qualifying channels are picked FIRST, so the window function runs over
-- their events only: every predicate is a property of the channel, and the
-- window partitions by channel, so dropping a channel cannot change the LAG of
-- a row that survives.
WITH node AS {{> vpn-nodes}},
vpn_channel AS (
  SELECT
    channel.id,
    channel.concrete_channel_id,
    payer.chain_key AS payer,
    relay.chain_key AS relay,
    CASE
      WHEN channel.source NOT IN (SELECT account_id FROM node) THEN 'upstream'
      ELSE 'downstream'
    END AS direction
  FROM channel
  JOIN account AS payer ON payer.id = channel.source
  JOIN account AS relay ON relay.id = channel.destination
  WHERE channel.destination IN (SELECT account_id FROM node)
    AND (
      channel.source NOT IN (SELECT account_id FROM node)
      OR payer.chain_key = ANY ({{list:exits}})
    )
),
ordered AS (
  -- The channel's own columns ride along with its events, so the result needs
  -- no second join back to vpn_channel — which the planner, unable to
  -- estimate how many channels qualify, would turn into a nested loop.
  SELECT
    vpn_channel.direction,
    vpn_channel.payer,
    vpn_channel.relay,
    vpn_channel.concrete_channel_id,
    cs.published_block,
    cs.published_tx_index,
    cs.published_log_index,
    cs.epoch,
    cs.ticket_index,
    LAG(cs.epoch) OVER w AS previous_epoch,
    LAG(cs.ticket_index) OVER w AS previous_ticket_index
  FROM channel_state AS cs
  JOIN vpn_channel ON vpn_channel.id = cs.channel_id
  WHERE cs.corrupted_state = FALSE
    AND cs.reorg_correction = FALSE
  WINDOW w AS (
    PARTITION BY cs.channel_id
    ORDER BY cs.published_block, cs.published_tx_index, cs.published_log_index
  )
)
SELECT
  direction,
  payer,
  relay,
  concrete_channel_id AS channel,
  published_block AS block,
  published_tx_index AS tx_index,
  published_log_index AS log_index,
  ticket_index - previous_ticket_index AS tickets
FROM ordered
WHERE previous_ticket_index IS NOT NULL
  AND epoch = previous_epoch
  AND ticket_index > previous_ticket_index

queries.title: Winning probability history
queries.description: Fragment: the winning probability in force over each range of blocks, from the oracle logs.
queries.sql:
-- The winning probability in force over each range of blocks.
--
-- Each update in {{> oracle-updates}} holds from its block until the next
-- one's. Blocks before the first update have no probability on record: they
-- match no row here, and the queries that join this price them at zero rather
-- than guess. With no history at all, the one value chain_info has covers
-- every block (or 1 when that is unset either).
WITH update AS (
  SELECT
    block_number,
    tx_index,
    log_index,
    {{> decode-win-prob(value)}} AS probability
  FROM {{> oracle-updates}} AS oracle
  WHERE kind = 'win-prob'
)
SELECT
  block_number AS from_block,
  COALESCE(
    LEAD(block_number) OVER (ORDER BY block_number, tx_index, log_index),
    9223372036854775807
  ) AS to_block,
  probability
FROM update
UNION ALL
SELECT
  0,
  9223372036854775807,
  COALESCE(
    (
      SELECT NULLIF(GREATEST(min_incoming_ticket_win_prob, 0), 0)
      FROM chain_info
      ORDER BY id
      LIMIT 1
    ),
    1
  )
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM update)

queries.title: VPN traffic
queries.description: Every VPN redemption, dated, with its direction, payer, relay and data volume.
queries.sql:
-- Every Gnosis VPN redemption, dated and converted to data volume.
--
-- One row per redemption from {{> vpn-redemptions}}: upstream (a client paying
-- a relay) and downstream (a configured exit paying a relay for the answer).
-- Most of the dashboard is drawn from this one result: volume, redemptions,
-- the hour-of-week grids, the relay breakdowns, the client ranking and each
-- client's own record.
--
-- Volume: a redemption pays for one winning ticket, and with winning
-- probability p a winner stands for 1/p tickets of 650 bytes each, so it
-- accounts for 650 / (2^30 × p) GB at the p in force at its block. Before the
-- oracle's first update p is unknown, and the redemption counts with no volume.
--
-- Dates come from {{> block-time(block)}}: estimated at five seconds a
-- block, counted back from the last indexed block.
SELECT
  {{> block-time(r.block)}} AS redeemed_at,
  ({{> block-time(r.block)}})::date AS day,
  r.block,
  r.direction,
  {{> hex(r.payer)}} AS payer,
  {{> hex(r.relay)}} AS relay,
  r.tickets,
  COALESCE(w.probability, 0) AS win_probability,
  CASE
    WHEN w.probability > 0 THEN 650::float8 / 1073741824 / w.probability
    ELSE 0
  END AS gigabytes
FROM {{> vpn-redemptions}} AS r
LEFT JOIN {{> win-probability}} AS w
  ON r.block >= w.from_block AND r.block < w.to_block
ORDER BY r.block, r.tx_index, r.log_index

queries.title: Client activity
queries.description: Each day each client was active — by redemption or by being deployed — with its deployment day.
queries.sql:
-- Each day each VPN client was active, with when it was deployed.
--
-- A client ({{> vpn-clients}}) is active on a day when a relay redeemed one of
-- its tickets that day, or when it was deployed that day — so a new client
-- counts at once rather than only after its first redemption. One row per
-- client and day:
--
--   kind          `new` on the deployment day, `returning` on any other
--   redemptions   0 on a deployment day with no traffic
--   deployed_on   the client's deployment day, on every row
--
-- Feeds the active-user counts, new versus returning, and the deployment
-- cohorts.
WITH deployment AS (
  SELECT
    client,
    ({{> block-time(deployed_block)}})::date AS deployed_on
  FROM {{> vpn-clients}} AS clients
),
redeemed AS (
  SELECT
    r.payer AS client,
    ({{> block-time(r.block)}})::date AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS redemptions
  FROM {{> vpn-redemptions}} AS r
  WHERE r.direction = 'upstream'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
active AS (
  SELECT client, day, redemptions FROM redeemed
  UNION ALL
  SELECT client, deployed_on, 0 FROM deployment
)
SELECT
  {{> hex(active.client)}} AS client,
  active.day,
  deployment.deployed_on,
  CASE WHEN active.day = deployment.deployed_on THEN 'new' ELSE 'returning' END AS kind,
  SUM(active.redemptions)::integer AS redemptions
FROM active
LEFT JOIN deployment ON deployment.client = active.client
GROUP BY active.client, active.day, deployment.deployed_on
ORDER BY active.day, client

queries.title: Client deployments
queries.description: Every VPN client deployment, newest first.
queries.sql:
-- Every VPN client deployment ({{> vpn-clients}}), newest first.
SELECT
  {{> block-time(deployed_block)}} AS deployed_at,
  ({{> block-time(deployed_block)}})::date AS deployed_on,
  deployed_block AS block,
  {{> hex(client)}} AS client
FROM {{> vpn-clients}} AS clients
ORDER BY deployed_block DESC, account_id DESC

queries.title: Recent redemptions
queries.description: The 500 most recent client redemptions, with their channel.
queries.sql:
-- The 500 most recent client redemptions, with the channel they were on.
--
-- The same population as the upstream rows of vpn-traffic — a client paying
-- an announced relay — but read newest first and capped, because it is the
-- only result that needs the channel id, and carrying a 64-character id on
-- every row of the full history would cost far more than this feed shows.
SELECT
  {{> block-time(r.block)}} AS redeemed_at,
  r.block,
  {{> hex(r.payer)}} AS client,
  {{> hex(r.relay)}} AS relay,
  '0x' || r.channel AS channel,
  r.tickets
FROM {{> vpn-redemptions}} AS r
WHERE r.direction = 'upstream'
ORDER BY r.block DESC, r.tx_index DESC, r.log_index DESC
LIMIT 500

queries.title: Network state
queries.description: Accounts, safes, open channels and balances at the last indexed block.
queries.sql:
-- The network as it stands at the last indexed block: one row.
--
-- Balances are 32-byte big-endian integers in wei, summed as exact numerics
-- ({{> uint256(balance)}}).
WITH amount AS (
  SELECT 'channel' AS kind, {{> uint256(balance)}} AS wei FROM channel_current
  WHERE status = 1 AND corrupted_state = FALSE
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'safe', {{> uint256(balance)}} FROM hopr_balance
  WHERE address IN (SELECT address FROM hopr_safe_contract)
)
SELECT
  (SELECT last_indexed_block FROM chain_info ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) AS indexed_block,
  {{> block-time((SELECT last_indexed_block FROM chain_info ORDER BY id LIMIT 1))}} AS indexed_at,
  COALESCE((SELECT version FROM schema_version ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1), 'unknown') AS schema_version,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM account) AS accounts,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hopr_safe_contract) AS safes,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_current WHERE status = 1 AND corrupted_state = FALSE) AS open_channels,
  COALESCE((SELECT ROUND(SUM(wei)) FROM amount WHERE kind = 'channel'), 0) AS channel_balance,
  COALESCE((SELECT ROUND(SUM(wei)) FROM amount WHERE kind = 'safe'), 0) AS safe_balance

queries.title: Ticket parameters
queries.description: Current winning probability, ticket price and ticket value.
queries.sql:
-- The oracle values as they stand: winning probability, ticket price, and
-- what a ticket is worth for one remaining hop (price ÷ probability). One row.
--
-- The newest update of each in {{> oracle-updates}}, so the figures match the
-- history the volume is priced with; both are null when the oracle has never
-- been indexed. Per network only: each network sets its own price and
-- probability, so a combined figure would be a fiction.
WITH latest_probability AS (
  SELECT {{> decode-win-prob(value)}} AS value
  FROM {{> oracle-updates}} AS oracle
  WHERE kind = 'win-prob'
  ORDER BY block_number DESC, tx_index DESC, log_index DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
latest_price AS (
  SELECT {{> uint256(value)}} AS wei
  FROM {{> oracle-updates}} AS oracle
  WHERE kind = 'ticket-price'
  ORDER BY block_number DESC, tx_index DESC, log_index DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  (SELECT value FROM latest_probability) AS win_probability,
  (SELECT ROUND(wei) FROM latest_price) AS ticket_price,
  (
    SELECT ROUND(latest_price.wei / latest_probability.value::numeric)
    FROM latest_price, latest_probability
    WHERE latest_probability.value > 0
  ) AS ticket_value

queries.title: Indexed contracts
queries.description: The contracts this index subscribes to, by role.
queries.sql:
-- The contracts this index subscribes to, named by the events they emit.
--
-- Blokli records one row per (contract, event topic) it watches, so the
-- distinct addresses are the contracts indexed and the topics — 32-byte event
-- signature hashes — say what each one is.
WITH role (topic, name) AS (
  VALUES
    ('ed22f34d154d253a7f6fd477439be59080a1554aa0d0642686d64223ab544c8a', 'Channels'),
    ('004c0177ad15bb302b4419e9ac96065d6f436e0f61972f97bbe272834c40f934', 'Channels'),
    ('197bba684a6afb7ba24f1d265605414b1d0051a6e295d6ff7b6e78e870d7a7f0', 'Channels'),
    ('c4df5ba16814838ab2618829d68f8623bb897302f24dbdba2279dbe45adb3d14', 'Announcements'),
    ('11d94653de52fc143887956fe4b5e4120a850b1300ece0533dee6bd8ff91f732', 'Announcements'),
    ('a4de30a528becadf82649d1395c0e30dd18ae35b5a96ce71e9295bb14bc9f3bc', 'Announcements'),
    ('776da40cbf2c223552661bd48502ceb72409b3362bb0c66d8989bd7e20e4497d', 'Node safe registry'),
    ('1eb3e9b31552ebe06015df6569e31abbec0e73a88c3ccdd9fead65c4378b4e50', 'Node safe registry'),
    ('2c906e9f9056ce9dab322be95fe710c2ecfa369bf6bf530bc81ced25caee90e1', 'Service registry'),
    ('38a84f1ca3cac973fcc30eeaccfd5a063993a9bd564530c4790ef60291c6b161', 'Service registry'),
    ('d4c5e06b1ae097ba02372652a7adaa6e4a8e00be527497a3ad0ebc3f761ef3fb', 'Ticket price oracle'),
    ('02728c4a80373f4765559dc3a046edea88186424827238bb46245668315d3800', 'Winning probability oracle'),
    ('06b541ddaa720db2b10a4d0cdac39b8d360425fc073085fac19bc82614677987', 'wxHOPR token'),
    ('f4caeb2d6ca8932a215a353d0703c326ec2d81fc68170f320eb2ab49e9df61f9', 'wxHOPR token'),
    ('83a5c31bfee49d254d95e3946d8e8434e5975382fa8b849182db9e251aaaaa26', 'Node stake factory'),
    ('141df868a6331af528e38c83b7aa03edc19be66e37ae67f9285bf4f8e3c6a1a8', 'Safe'),
    ('442e715f626346e8c54381002da614f62bee8d27386535b2521ec8540898556e', 'Safe')
),
contract AS (
  SELECT address, ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT encode(topic, 'hex') ORDER BY encode(topic, 'hex')) AS topics
  FROM log_topic_info
  GROUP BY address
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(
    (
      SELECT role.name
      FROM unnest(contract.topics) WITH ORDINALITY AS t (topic, position)
      JOIN role ON role.topic = t.topic
      ORDER BY t.position
      LIMIT 1
    ),
    'Indexed contract'
  ) AS role,
  {{> hex(contract.address)}} AS contract
FROM contract
ORDER BY role, contract

options.caption: configured exits seen paying a relay
of the hour-of-week pattern, all time

config.sql:
-- One minus half the total variation between the two directions' shares of
-- volume by weekday and hour: 1 when the grids match, 0 when they share no hour.
WITH cell AS (
  SELECT direction,
         EXTRACT(isodow FROM redeemed_at) AS weekday,
         EXTRACT(hour FROM redeemed_at) AS hour,
         SUM(gigabytes) AS gigabytes
  FROM {{result}}
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
),
share AS (
  SELECT direction, weekday, hour,
         gigabytes / NULLIF(SUM(gigabytes) OVER (PARTITION BY direction), 0) AS share
  FROM cell
),
up AS (SELECT * FROM share WHERE direction = 'upstream' AND share IS NOT NULL),
down AS (SELECT * FROM share WHERE direction = 'downstream' AND share IS NOT NULL)
SELECT CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM up) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM down)
           THEN 1 - SUM(ABS(COALESCE(up.share, 0) - COALESCE(down.share, 0))) / 2
       END AS agreement
FROM up FULL JOIN down ON up.weekday = down.weekday AND up.hour = down.hour

-- Clients grouped by the month they were deployed (from January 2026), and for
-- each month since, the share of the group a relay redeemed tickets for.
WITH member AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT network, client, DATE_TRUNC('month', deployed_on)::date AS cohort
  FROM {{result}}
  WHERE deployed_on >= DATE '2026-01-01'
),
size AS (
  SELECT cohort, COUNT(*) AS clients FROM member GROUP BY cohort
),
active AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT network, client, DATE_TRUNC('month', day)::date AS month
  FROM {{result}}
  WHERE redemptions > 0
),
grid AS (
  SELECT size.cohort, size.clients, offset_month
  FROM size,
       generate_series(
         0,
         ((EXTRACT(year FROM CURRENT_DATE) - EXTRACT(year FROM size.cohort)) * 12
           + EXTRACT(month FROM CURRENT_DATE) - EXTRACT(month FROM size.cohort))::integer
       ) AS offset_month
)
SELECT TO_CHAR(grid.cohort, 'YYYY-MM') || ' · ' || grid.clients AS cohort,
       grid.offset_month AS month,
       COUNT(active.client)::float8 / grid.clients AS share
FROM grid
JOIN member ON member.cohort = grid.cohort
LEFT JOIN active
  ON active.network = member.network
 AND active.client = member.client
 AND active.month = (grid.cohort + MAKE_INTERVAL(months => grid.offset_month))::date
GROUP BY grid.cohort, grid.clients, grid.offset_month
ORDER BY grid.cohort, grid.offset_month

dashboards.title: Gnosis VPN
dashboards.description: Who uses Gnosis VPN, how much traffic it carries and where, read from the HOPR network’s on-chain ticket redemptions.

A user is a VPN client — an account that bound a key but never announced an address, so it is not relay infrastructure. Upstream volume is derived from the redemptions on client channels, priced at the winning probability in force at each block; downstream is what the configured exits pay relays for the return path.
Each point counts distinct clients over the 30 days before it.
Daily up to a month, weekly beyond. Upstream is paid for by the client and attributable to it; downstream is paid for by the exit, whose channels name no client.
Exits are configured per network on the Exits page.
An answer follows its request within seconds, so one session should shade both grids the same way.
Who showed up each day, and when during the day the network carries traffic.

Read a row left to right: it follows the clients deployed that month, and each square is the share of them relaying traffic that many months later. Month 0 is an activation rate. Not affected by the range.
Share of volume in the chosen direction by weekday and hour, UTC.
Estimated client traffic carried by each relay.
Upstream volume.
Split by the relay each client (upstream) or exit (downstream) paid. Downstream names no client, so it is a relay breakdown, never a client one.

Current network minimum
Cost of relaying one packet, one hop

Who used the network and when each client first appeared. Volume is upstream only — the traffic the client itself paid for. Pick a client to open its record.
The latest client redemptions, newest first. Upstream only — a downstream redemption is paid by an exit and names no client.

Blokli appends a channel state row per on-chain event, and only TicketRedeemed advances the ticket index, so a row whose index advances is a redemption. A client paying a relay is upstream; a configured exit paying a relay is the return path, downstream. Each redemption accounts for 650 / (2^30 × p) GB, where p is the winning probability from the oracle’s update history at that block. Every figure here is a saved query and a chart over its result: open them in the studio to see exactly how.

dashboards.title: Gnosis VPN client
dashboards.description: One VPN client’s record: when it was deployed, what it used, and which relays it paid.

options.note: A client leaves no trace of its own on chain: what is visible is a relay redeeming a ticket the client issued. First and last seen are the bounds of that trace. Open a client from the Gnosis VPN dashboard, or set one in the address bar.
